title: deterministic-slice-simulator-for-staged-promote-and-auto-remediate
author: Rhea Gupta
description: Motivation: We frequently need to reproduce subtle canary regressions that only surface for particular traffic slices (session cohorts, geo/time windows, client SDK versions). This PR introduces a deterministic slice simulator and a staged-promote workflow that enables repeatable shadow->canary promotions and automated remediate actions when smoke assertions fail. Design overview: 1) deterministically sample traffic by a reproducible 'slice key' derived from request attributes; 2) a simulator engine that can replay N synthetic or historical requests through the exact routing and pre-processing layers used in production; 3) a staged-promote controller that can promote a shadow slice to an isolated canary fraction with smoke assertions, and optionally run a fast bisect to find offending model or prompt changes; 4) an auto-remediate policy that consumes rollback credits and triggers either a rollback or an isolation quarantine plus a snapshot for postmortem. Key benefits: reproduces flakey regressions locally and in CI, enables safe fast-promote for slices with smoke gating, shortens MTTI by auto-remediation and reproducible bisect traces. Implementation details: - New package redwood/lifecycle/slice_simulator: deterministic hashing, replay harness, pluggable request fixtures. - Controller changes in redwood/controllers/promote_controller: added stagedPromote API, staged state machine (shadow->probe->canary->promote/fail). - Telemetry: emit slice_id and replay_trace_id across tracing spans; new metrics: slice_simulator.replays_total, staged_promote.success_rate, staged_promote.auto_remediate_count. - Smoke assertions: declarative JSON schema in redwood/configs/smoke_assertions/* that supports latency, top-k divergence, and distributional drift checks. - Rollback playbook: integrated with existing rollback-orchestrator to consume rollback credits and to attach snapshot artifacts for repro. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for deterministic sampling and hashing (edge cases for malformed headers). - Integration harness that runs replayed traffic through compiled runtimes in a mocked routing environment. - E2E smoke test that runs a shadow->promote cycle against a small model variant on CI. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of traffic slices for 48 hours, gradual increase based on staged_promote.success_rate and absence of drift alerts. Safety gates: automatic hold if top-k divergence > configured threshold, immediate rollback if smoke assertion fails twice within 10 minutes for same slice_id. Related work and notes: complements existing traffic-hydrator and shadow-capture features; does not replace full cohort orchestration, but provides a deterministic sandbox to reproduce cohort-specific failures. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests added, [x] integration tests added, [x] telemetry hooks, [x] docs updated (redwood-docs/lifecycle). How to exercise locally: make a fixtures directory under redwood/dev-fixtures; run `make slice-replay FIXTURE=...` to see deterministic request ordering and trace ids. Commands for CI: `bazel test //redwood/lifecycle/...` and `./scripts/run_e2e_staged_promote.sh`. Migration notes: smoke_assertions defaults to conservative thresholds; operators can opt-in per-tenant using the new stagedPromotePolicy CRD. Backwards compatibility: non-adopting tenants have no change in behavior. Expected impact: short-term increased CI runtime for e2e suite (opt-in), long-term decrease in incident resolution time for canary regressions.
commits: init: add slice_simulator package and deterministic hashing
controller: staged promote state machine and API
docs: lifecycle guide and operator notes
review_conversation: Kenji: Can we ensure the deterministic hash is stable across minor SDK version bumps? R: We compute slice_key from a whitelist of attributes and include sdk_version only if configured; default avoids sdk_version to preserve stability.
Maya: The smoke assertion DSL looks powerful but complex; can we ship a simple sane default? R: Added default_staged_policy.yaml with conservative thresholds and examples.
Liam: CI e2e runtime increased; can we make the e2e optional per PR? R: Added opt-in env flag to skip e2e in fast CI; nightly runs still exercise full e2e.
Kenji (approve): Looks good after fixes to hashing edge cases.
Maya (approve): Verified telemetry traces and smoke assertion behavior in staging.
release_notes: Added deterministic slice simulator and staged-promote workflow with smoke gating and auto-remediate policy. Operators must opt-in to stagedPromotePolicy; default policy is conservative.
notes_for_oncall: If a staged promote triggers auto-remediate, rollback-orchestrator will emit an alert with replay_trace_id; use `make slice-replay` with that id to reproduce. Monitor staged_promote.success_rate and slice_simulator.replays_total in the rollout dashboard.
